blocks.text: **ставить** — **поставить**: to put, to place in a vertical position or on the base of the object; to park (a car). Phrases meaning direction are used to denote the place where something is put ("**на**" + Acc., "**в**" + Acc., etc.): *Я поставил лампу на стол. Я поставил автомобиль в гараж.* However, when something is put in a wide or open space, phrases meaning location are mostly used: *Я поставил автомобиль на площади.*
**класть** — **положить**: to put, to place, to lay in a horizontal position: *Я кладу книги в ящик. Я кладу книги на стол.*
**садиться** — **сесть**: to sit down. Literally **садиться** means "to seat oneself".

It implies movement to a "seat" and, therefore, answers the question "**куда**?": *Садитесь на стул. Садитесь в кресло.* The same is applicable to the verbs **ложиться** — **лечь** (to lie down) and **становиться** — **стать** (to take a standing position).

The verbs "**сидеть**", "**лежать**" and "**стоять**" form their perfective aspect by adding prefix "**по**-": **посидеть**, **полежать**, **постоять**. These perfective verbs denote a completed action of limited duration: *Я хочу посидеть здесь 5 минут.*
From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lessons 42, 68.
Further sentences, so that every pattern above is practised: from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR), with their English.

exercises.prompt: Male chauvinists believe themselves to be superior to any woman.
exercises.why: **ставить → ставят** — present tense, 3rd person plural: ending -ят belongs to the second (и) conjugation.
**сидеть → сидел** — past tense, masc.: drop -ть, add -л.

exercises.q: Я ___ (сесть) за барную стойку рядом с Томом.
exercises.prompt: I sat at the bar with Tom.

exercises.q: Он ___ (сидеть) за столом в окружении фальшивых друзей и бесстыдных женщин.
exercises.prompt: He sits at a table, surrounded by false friends and shameless women.
exercises.why: **сидеть → сидит** — present tense, 3rd person singular: ending -ит belongs to the second (и) conjugation.

exercises.prompt: Tom sat alone at the counter.
exercises.why: **сидеть → сидел** — past tense, masc.: drop -ть, add -л.

exercises.q: Инна ___ (лечь) под балдахин и крепко уснула.
exercises.prompt: Inna lay down under the canopy and fell fast asleep.
They put the lamp on the nightstand.
exercises.why: **поставить → поставили** — past tense, plural: drop -ть, add -ли.

exercises.q: Он ___ (сесть) на велосипед и умчался прочь.
exercises.prompt: He got on his bike and sped off.

exercises.why: **ложиться → ложится** — present tense, 3rd person singular: ending -ит belongs to the second (и) conjugation.

exercises.q: Согни салфетки и ___ (положить) у каждой тарелки по одной.
exercises.prompt: Fold the napkins and put one by each plate.

exercises.q: Том ___ (сесть) на своего коня и ускакал.
exercises.prompt: Tom mounted his horse and rode off.
He deposited the prize money in the bank.
exercises.why: **положить → положил** — past tense, masc.: drop -ть, add -л.

exercises.q: Я не ___ (ставить) перед собой нереальные цели.
exercises.prompt: I don't set myself unrealistic goals.

exercises.q: Посыпьте рыбу солью и перцем и ___ (положить) её поверх овощей.
exercises.prompt: Sprinkle the fish with salt and pepper and lay it on top of the vegetables.
exercises.why: **положить → положите** — perfective verb, 2nd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Lie down on the examination table.
exercises.why: **ложиться → Ложитесь** — present tense, 2nd person plural: ending -ите belongs to the second (и) conjugation.
